headline: MS Dhoni Retires From the IPL After 19 Years, Will Mentor CSK in 2027
subheadline: Chennai Super Kings confirmed the end of Dhoni's playing career hours before the retention deadline. The five-title captain stays on as Team Mentor from IPL 2027.
body:
• Chennai Super Kings announced on Tuesday, November 17, that MS Dhoni has retired from the Indian Premier League as a player, ending a 19-year IPL career that began in the tournament's inaugural season in 2008.
  • Dhoni, 45, will stay with the franchise as Team Mentor from IPL 2027. CSK's release carried no comment from Dhoni himself and named no successor.
  • He led CSK to five IPL titles — 2010, 2011, 2018, 2021 and 2023, the joint-most by any captain — and two Champions League T20 titles, and finishes as the franchise's most-capped player with 272 appearances and 5,314 runs for the Super Kings.
  • The announcement came three hours before the deadline for franchises to name retained and released players ahead of the December 16 auction in Goa, Cricinfo reported.

MS Dhoni's playing career in the Indian Premier League is over. Chennai Super Kings announced on Tuesday that their former captain has retired from the IPL ahead of the 2027 season and will begin a new chapter with the franchise as Team Mentor from IPL 2027.

"MS Dhoni will begin a new chapter with the Chennai Super Kings as Team Mentor from IPL 2027," CSK said in a release, according to The Times of India. The statement carried no comment from Dhoni himself, and the franchise gave no details of the mentor role beyond the title and its start. The announcement came three hours before the deadline for teams to name their retained and released players ahead of the 16 December auction in Goa, Cricinfo reported.

"There is no CSK without MS Dhoni. For nearly two decades, we have walked and grown alongside each other, through triumphs, setbacks and everything in between."

— N Srinivasan, CSK co-owner

The record he leaves

Dhoni joined CSK in 2008 and spent 17 seasons with the franchise; the other two of his 19 IPL years came with Rising Pune Super Giant in 2016 and 2017, while CSK were banned from the league. He finishes his IPL career with 5,439 runs at an average of 38.30 and a strike rate of 137.45, according to Cricinfo. For CSK alone, he is the second-highest run-scorer with 5,314 runs and the most-capped player in the franchise's history with 272 appearances, The Times of India reported.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=6hl08H8jqAI

As captain, he led the Super Kings to five IPL titles — in 2010, 2011, 2018, 2021 and 2023 — the joint-most by any captain, apart from two Champions League T20 titles, the most by any skipper. The World Cup-winning captain had already retired from international cricket in August 2020. He did not play a single match in IPL 2026 despite remaining part of the CSK squad, and the retirement closes the question that had hung over the franchise's retention planning for next season.

"This will always be his home"

CSK co-owner N Srinivasan, who brought Dhoni to Chennai at the league's first auction, paid the central tribute. "Our relationship is as strong as it is because of one reason: we don't question intentions. That trust is what made this journey possible. In 2008, I insisted that Dhoni should be part of CSK... It turns out that's the best decision I took. Not because of all his achievements for the franchise, but for the kind of human he is," Srinivasan said. "Dhoni will always be a part of our identity. This will always be his home."

What happens next

CSK must now name their retained and released players without the most successful captain in their history on the playing list, ahead of the December 16 auction in Goa. The franchise's announcement did not name a successor as the on-field leader for IPL 2027, and it did not set out what the mentor role will involve day to day. What is settled is the association itself: the player who defined the franchise from its first season will still be in its dugout when IPL 2027 begins — in the mentor's seat, not at the toss.
diaspora_angle: Dhoni's retirement closes the playing career of the cricketer most diaspora fans grew up watching; his mentor role keeps him in the IPL dugout for 2027, when CSK will tour global fan attention without him on the field.
image_caption: MS Dhoni, in his Chennai Super Kings No. 7 jersey and wicketkeeping gloves, walks off during an IPL match. CSK announced on November 17, 2026 that Dhoni has retired as a player and will serve as the team's mentor from IPL 2027.
key_takeaways: MS Dhoni retires from IPL after 19 years, becoming a mentor for CSK in 2027.
He led CSK to five IPL titles and two Champions League T20 titles.
Dhoni finishes as CSK's most-capped player with 272 appearances and 5,314 runs.
CSK has not named a successor for Dhoni's captaincy ahead of the December auction.
N Srinivasan praised Dhoni's impact on CSK and their strong relationship.
